{"base_revision":null,"capture_truncated":false,"diff":false,"live_changed":false,"next_offset":226,"offset":116,"order_changed":false,"revision":"ax-11854777484584763333:1","text":"paragraph "Augusta Ada King, Countess of Lovelace (née Byron; 10 December 1815 – 27 November 1852), also known as Ada Lovelace, was an English mathematician and writer chiefly known for work on Charles Babbage's"
[ax-5522222734164509727] link "née"
[ax-14451142165861724624] link "mathematician"
[ax-11990888914609983973] link "writer"
[ax-3532300359061971565] link "Charles Babbage"
[ax-6939472827169922962] link "computer"
[ax-7210997671381206217] link "analytical engine"
[ax-8975844578461234101] link "computer programmer"
paragraph "Lovelace was the only legitimate child of poet Lord Byron and reformer Anne Isabella Milbanke.[2] Lord Byron separated from his wife a month after Ada was born, and died when she was eight. Although o"
[ax-7642889781631918907] link "legitimate child"
[ax-8609916022916223456] link "Lord Byron"
[ax-15499600999312922788] link "Anne Isabella Milbanke"
[ax-5683245923110320118] link "[2]"
[ax-3103570399340521214] link "assiduously"
[ax-13697665781047376242] link "William King"
[ax-16068042560596729215] link "Baron"
[ax-9169668492931294747] link "Earl of Lovelace"
[ax-16519154508152307517] link "Baron Lovelaces"
[ax-12496430570355755708] link "[3]"
paragraph "Lovelace's educational and social exploits brought her into contact with scientists such as Andrew Crosse, Charles Babbage, David Brewster, Charles Wheatstone and Michael Faraday, and the author Charl"
[ax-6530787473850407732] link "Andrew Crosse"
[ax-514381571581783551] link "David Brewster"
[ax-14940575485281984608] link "Charles Wheatstone"
[ax-14853377189169967251] link "Michael Faraday"
[ax-2583976796937803614] link "Charles Dickens"
[ax-615801383990380717] link "[4]"
[ax-9610232666079657732] link "Metaphysician"
[ax-17527791525494005116] link "[5]"
paragraph "At age 18, Lovelace's mathematical talents led her to a long working relationship and friendship with fellow British mathematician Charles Babbage. She was particularly interested in Babbage's work on"
[ax-13849321513035120927] link "Charles Babbage's Saturday night soirées"
[ax-2356899007554613056] link "[6]"
[ax-8271601015963498304] link "Mary Somerville"
[ax-5498043677294363005] link "Turing-complete"
[ax-8453330001045449633] link "an article"
[ax-16056080565566585582] link "Luigi Menabrea"
[ax-15642411989249771252] link "seven long explanatory notes"
[ax-2318514579803428328] link "Bernoulli numbers"
[ax-12240387592154486261] link "computer program"
paragraph "She developed a vision of the capability of computers to go beyond mere calculating or number-crunching, while many others, including Babbage, focused only on those capabilities.[7] Lovelace was the f"
[ax-12834932733830477948] link "calculating"
[ax-18424467554698382763] link "[7]"
[ax-16862344106311039715] link "arithmetical"
[ax-2304967064938079746] link "music"
[ax-17159260193254143279] link "[8]"
[ax-6094103250982331017] link "programming language"
heading "Biography"
heading "Childhood"
paragraph "Lord Byron expected his child to be a \"glorious boy\" and was disappointed when Lady Byron gave birth to a girl.[9] The child was named after Byron's half-sister, Augusta Leigh, and was called \"Ada\" by"
[ax-5419237773684306939] link "Lord Byron"
[ax-8281544174189444338] link "Lady Byron"
[ax-8919660273522123050] link "[9]"
[ax-4508394545204194785] link "Augusta Leigh"
[ax-11037340432931648193] link "[10]"
[ax-7777200734351916789] link "Kirkby Mallory"
[ax-721803177596651397] link "[9]"
[ax-385825712431150305] link "[11]"
[ax-8711979748441830966] link "[12]"
[ax-445593094751357764] link ""
text "Ada Byron, aged four"
paragraph "On 21 April, Lord Byron signed the deed of separation, although very reluctantly, and left England for good a few days later.[13] Aside from an acrimonious separation, Lady Byron continued throughout "
[ax-12643804208977305210] link "deed of separation"
[ax-17506024020922330539] link "[13]"
[ax-2929677218794580740] link "[14]"
[ax-4499225701856334098] link "[15]"
[ax-11996003295803903793] link "[16]"
[ax-6279351395667662422] link ""
text "Ada Byron, aged seven, by , 1822,"
[ax-17100397992920556519] link "Alfred d'Orsay"
[ax-5962422039013533193] link "Somerville College, Oxford"
paragraph "Lovelace did not have a close relationship with her mother. She was often left in the care of her maternal grandmother Judith, Hon. Lady Milbanke, who doted on her. However, because of societal attitu"
[ax-4774759182775345656] link "[17]"
[ax-7375216427690421113] link "[18]"
[ax-9057311581206885211] link "[19]"
[ax-12081507871543247113] link ""
text "Ada Byron, aged seventeen, 1832"
paragraph "Lovelace was often ill, beginning in early childhood. At the age of eight, she experienced headaches that obscured her vision.[10] In June 1829, she was paralyzed after a bout of measles. She was subj"
[ax-15406959897083661402] link "[10]"
[ax-480422801993017438] link "measles"
blockquote "When Ada was twelve years old, this future \"Lady Fairy\", as Charles Babbage affectionately called her, decided she wanted to fly. Ada Byron went about the project methodically, thoughtfully, with imag"
paragraph "When Ada was twelve years old, this future \"Lady Fairy\", as Charles Babbage affectionately called her, decided she wanted to fly. Ada Byron went about the project methodically, thoughtfully, with imag"
[ax-7517817007816698473] link "anatomy of birds"
[ax-6470488616433837075] link "[8]"
paragraph "Ada Byron had an affair with a tutor in early 1833. She tried to elope with him after she was caught, but the tutor's relatives recognised her and contacted her mother. Lady Byron and her friends cove"
[ax-8160521062408820234] link "[20]"
[ax-8686535062836187503] link "Allegra"
[ax-11519070058720057606] link "Claire Clairmont"
[ax-5048438615726838963] link "Elizabeth Medora Leigh"
[ax-7096942874200890082] link "[21]"
heading "Adult years"
[ax-12475565782823109694] link ""
text "Watercolor portrait of Ada Byron, by , c. 1835."
[ax-17500022755030697196] link "Alfred Edward Chalon"
[ax-15138307088771403813] link ""
text "Watercolour portrait of Ada King, Countess of Lovelace, , possibly by Alfred Edward Chalon"
text "1840"
paragraph "Lovelace became close friends with her tutor Mary Somerville, who introduced her to Charles Babbage in 1833. She had a strong respect and affection for Somerville,[22] and they corresponded for many y"
[ax-16971803039550421221] link "Mary Somerville"
[ax-8330809766415548602] link "[22]"
[ax-3333600568677074293] link "Andrew Crosse"
[ax-15993171156817812169] link "Sir David Brewster"
[ax-10621870950563922984] link "Charles Wheatstone"
[ax-761167246320784140] link "Michael Faraday"
[ax-8675793329655179895] link "Charles Dickens"

{"base_revision":null,"capture_truncated":false,"diff":false,"live_changed":false,"next_offset":226,"offset":116,"order_changed":false,"revision":"ax-11854777484584763333:1","text":"paragraph "Augusta Ada King, Countess of Lovelace (née Byron; 10 December 1815 – 27 November 1852), also known as Ada Lovelace, was an English mathematician and writer chiefly known for work on Charles Babbage's"
[ax-5522222734164509727] link "née"
[ax-14451142165861724624] link "mathematician"
[ax-11990888914609983973] link "writer"
[ax-3532300359061971565] link "Charles Babbage"
[ax-6939472827169922962] link "computer"
[ax-7210997671381206217] link "analytical engine"
[ax-8975844578461234101] link "computer programmer"
paragraph "Lovelace was the only legitimate child of poet Lord Byron and reformer Anne Isabella Milbanke.[2] Lord Byron separated from his wife a month after Ada was born, and died when she was eight. Although o"
[ax-7642889781631918907] link "legitimate child"
[ax-8609916022916223456] link "Lord Byron"
[ax-15499600999312922788] link "Anne Isabella Milbanke"
[ax-5683245923110320118] link "[2]"
[ax-3103570399340521214] link "assiduously"
[ax-13697665781047376242] link "William King"
[ax-16068042560596729215] link "Baron"
[ax-9169668492931294747] link "Earl of Lovelace"
[ax-16519154508152307517] link "Baron Lovelaces"
[ax-12496430570355755708] link "[3]"
paragraph "Lovelace's educational and social exploits brought her into contact with scientists such as Andrew Crosse, Charles Babbage, David Brewster, Charles Wheatstone and Michael Faraday, and the author Charl"
[ax-6530787473850407732] link "Andrew Crosse"
[ax-514381571581783551] link "David Brewster"
[ax-14940575485281984608] link "Charles Wheatstone"
[ax-14853377189169967251] link "Michael Faraday"
[ax-2583976796937803614] link "Charles Dickens"
[ax-615801383990380717] link "[4]"
[ax-9610232666079657732] link "Metaphysician"
[ax-17527791525494005116] link "[5]"
paragraph "At age 18, Lovelace's mathematical talents led her to a long working relationship and friendship with fellow British mathematician Charles Babbage. She was particularly interested in Babbage's work on"
[ax-13849321513035120927] link "Charles Babbage's Saturday night soirées"
[ax-2356899007554613056] link "[6]"
[ax-8271601015963498304] link "Mary Somerville"
[ax-5498043677294363005] link "Turing-complete"
[ax-8453330001045449633] link "an article"
[ax-16056080565566585582] link "Luigi Menabrea"
[ax-15642411989249771252] link "seven long explanatory notes"
[ax-2318514579803428328] link "Bernoulli numbers"
[ax-12240387592154486261] link "computer program"
paragraph "She developed a vision of the capability of computers to go beyond mere calculating or number-crunching, while many others, including Babbage, focused only on those capabilities.[7] Lovelace was the f"
[ax-12834932733830477948] link "calculating"
[ax-18424467554698382763] link "[7]"
[ax-16862344106311039715] link "arithmetical"
[ax-2304967064938079746] link "music"
[ax-17159260193254143279] link "[8]"
[ax-6094103250982331017] link "programming language"
heading "Biography"
heading "Childhood"
paragraph "Lord Byron expected his child to be a \"glorious boy\" and was disappointed when Lady Byron gave birth to a girl.[9] The child was named after Byron's half-sister, Augusta Leigh, and was called \"Ada\" by"
[ax-5419237773684306939] link "Lord Byron"
[ax-8281544174189444338] link "Lady Byron"
[ax-8919660273522123050] link "[9]"
[ax-4508394545204194785] link "Augusta Leigh"
[ax-11037340432931648193] link "[10]"
[ax-7777200734351916789] link "Kirkby Mallory"
[ax-721803177596651397] link "[9]"
[ax-385825712431150305] link "[11]"
[ax-8711979748441830966] link "[12]"
[ax-445593094751357764] link ""
text "Ada Byron, aged four"
paragraph "On 21 April, Lord Byron signed the deed of separation, although very reluctantly, and left England for good a few days later.[13] Aside from an acrimonious separation, Lady Byron continued throughout "
[ax-12643804208977305210] link "deed of separation"
[ax-17506024020922330539] link "[13]"
[ax-2929677218794580740] link "[14]"
[ax-4499225701856334098] link "[15]"
[ax-11996003295803903793] link "[16]"
[ax-6279351395667662422] link ""
text "Ada Byron, aged seven, by , 1822,"
[ax-17100397992920556519] link "Alfred d'Orsay"
[ax-5962422039013533193] link "Somerville College, Oxford"
paragraph "Lovelace did not have a close relationship with her mother. She was often left in the care of her maternal grandmother Judith, Hon. Lady Milbanke, who doted on her. However, because of societal attitu"
[ax-4774759182775345656] link "[17]"
[ax-7375216427690421113] link "[18]"
[ax-9057311581206885211] link "[19]"
[ax-12081507871543247113] link ""
text "Ada Byron, aged seventeen, 1832"
paragraph "Lovelace was often ill, beginning in early childhood. At the age of eight, she experienced headaches that obscured her vision.[10] In June 1829, she was paralyzed after a bout of measles. She was subj"
